title: 2.4.32 Print a Grid Pattern
description: Write a nested-loop program that prints a grid of at least 5x5, with the dimensions controlled by variables, not hardcoded loop bounds. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Declare the grid's dimensions as variables
steps.instructions: Declare a variable called rows and a variable called cols. Set each to a number of at least 5. Do not write the numbers directly into the loop headers: the loops must read them from these variables.

steps.title: Build the grid with a nested loop
steps.instructions: Write an outer for loop with counter row that runs while row is less than rows. Inside it, build a string called line, and write an inner for loop with counter col that runs while col is less than cols, appending a character (like "#" or "*") to line on every pass.

steps.title: Print each row
steps.instructions: After the inner loop closes, log line so each row of the grid prints on its own line. Change rows and cols to different values (still at least 5) and confirm the grid resizes without touching the loops themselves.

requirements.title: rows variable declared
requirements.description: A variable named rows is declared

requirements.title: cols variable declared
requirements.description: A variable named cols is declared

requirements.title: outer loop reads rows
requirements.description: An outer for loop (from 0) contains a nested inner for loop (from 0) whose bound is the cols variable, the outer's bound is the rows variable, and the row is logged after the inner loop closes (any consistent counter names accepted, e.g. i/j)

requirements.title: inner loop reads cols
requirements.description: The inner loop's condition compares its own counter against the cols variable, and the outer against rows, not hardcoded numbers (any consistent counter names accepted, e.g. i/j)
